flicker.note: 29% of 114 real clips fall outside the synthetic P1-P99 range [0.00236, 0.166] (29% below, 0% above). Real clips are steadier than the synthetic ones (real P5 0.001 vs synthetic P1 0.002). render.exposure_flicker already starts at 0, so the synthetic floor comes from the scenes themselves (aerosol growing or drifting through the view changes the frame mean); nothing to widen in the camera model.

motion_px.note: 43% of 114 real clips fall outside the synthetic P1-P99 range [0.0494, 51.4] (43% below, 0% above). Real cameras are steadier (real P5 0.01 px vs synthetic P1 0.05 px per 60 s). render.camera_shake_px already starts at 0 (now [0, 0.3]) but is drawn uniformly, so few synthetic clips are as steady as a rigid mount: make near-zero shake more common or lengthen render.camera_shake_tau_s (now [1, 30] s) so that frames stay correlated; part of the synthetic floor can also be aerosol motion that the phase correlation follows.
